canonical_text: Concept Cells v0.7 stores each memory as one concept cell on a whitened unit-ball geometry, firing per cell when a query clears that cell's threshold.
Concept Cells v0.8 adds an auditable SLM controller that classifies intent and proposes writes, while the response policy guarantees answers come only from fired memories or an explicit refusal.
Concept Cells v0.9 adds adversarial guardrails: rule and local-JSON controllers, prompt-injection resistance, silent refusal, and deleted memories that can no longer be cited.

Concept Cells v1.0-rc1 found that no single MiniLM activation threshold separates genuine paraphrases from one-word near-miss flips, giving a false-accept rate of 0.58 and unsupported-after-grounding of 0.29.

Concept Cells v1.0-rc2 keeps cells as fast candidate memory and adds a deterministic verifier that drives false-accept and unsupported-after-grounding to 0.0 with near-miss reject 1.0 and recall at k 1.0.
Concept Cells v1.0-final is reproducible offline: 63 tests pass, exp01 smoke passes, and exp10 through exp12 regenerate byte-identical result JSONs from a single validation script.
Known limitation: the verifier is deliberately conservative, so genuine paraphrases it cannot match are refused rather than grounded, and optional NLI verification stays deferred and opt-in.
Next research direction: expand verifier recall (v1.1 Exp 13 to 16) without weakening the rule that a deterministic REJECT can never be overridden, and only after the v1.0 freeze is reviewed.
